A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DPO Unchained research. The complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, references and appendices are readable and can be matched despite reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v3 Section 6, Figure 1 and Appendix X report original Gemma2 training experiments comparing non-convex losses with exponential loss on Alpaca Eval v2.

after.justification: v4 retains these original training experiments and their outcomes in Section 6, Figure 1 and Appendix III.

M1.justification: The three-component framework, PPPO construction and experimental loss remain unchanged. Machina lotteries are renamed MDM lotteries without changing their construction. The length-bias correction highlighted in v4 was already present in v3 Appendix Remark T.

E1.justification: Both versions train on Ultrafeedback-binarized and evaluate on Alpaca Eval v2. The expanded discussion of lotteries and abstention introduces no additional evaluated task, population or scenario.

E2.justification: Figure 1 retains exponential-loss training as the comparator for the same three non-convex loss settings. Table 1 retains its theoretical classification of DPO variants; the additional citations do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Both versions specify Gemma2_2B_IT, 200 training steps, batch size 8 and evaluation on Alpaca Eval v2 using gemini-2.5-flash-lite. The remaining training controls and testing procedures also match.

E4.justification: The same three-value loss-parameter comparison and accompanying loss plots are retained. The new graph illustrating an existing choice axiom supplies explanation, not an additional ablation, robustness test or empirical analysis.

E5.justification: Section 6 in both versions reports averaging over two runs. Neither version adds seed identities, confidence intervals, significance tests or other uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Figure 1 reports identical win rates against exponential loss: 44.60% for a=10, 54.50% for a=6 and 53.00% for a=3. The settings, ranking and qualitative observation about potential benefits of non-convexity are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 2.2 corrects the Bregman-divergence definition from subtracting phi(u) to subtracting phi(v). Appendix III also qualifies exponential loss's strong convexity by specifying a right-bounded domain. The principal theorems, assumptions and appendix proofs otherwise match after renumbering.

C1.justification: The conclusion newly asserts compatibility with orthogonal extensions involving marginal/posterior optimization, noise handling and time-varying preferences. The central claims about disentanglement, non-convex losses, margins and length correction remain unchanged; the extended title emphasizes an existing claim.

C2.justification: New Section 5.5 distinguishes local incomparability from outside-option rejection and discusses the relationship to random utility theory. The new impact statement addresses bias in normative assumptions, while Appendix III explicitly cautions that the toy experiment cannot support firm conclusions about the proposed optimization/generalization tradeoff.

D1.justification: v3 Appendix X and v4 Appendix III provide the same hardware, optimizer, learning rate, clipping, input-length and training-budget information. No new implementation instructions or code/data-access information are supplied.

R1.justification: v4 adds Davidson and Marschak, Luce and Raiffa, Train, Bartlett and Mendelson, and Rakhlin et al. These support expanded lottery attribution, outside-option positioning and loss-design motivation. The existing positioning relative to DPO variants is retained.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites expand the introduction, Section 3.2, conclusion and experimental motivation. v4 extends the title, introduces MDM terminology, adds Section 5.5 and an impact statement, and subdivides the explanatory appendix. Most exposition and proof organization remain intact.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from a single-column report to a two-column conference layout, substantially altering typography, wrapping and display placement. v4 adds Figure 3 illustrating the choice axiom and substantially reduces existing loss-plot sizes; the old appendix Figure 3 becomes Figure 4.

improvement.justification: v4 modestly improves precision and interpretability through the corrected Bregman definition, clearer attribution, the axiom diagram and explicit limits on the toy experiment. The core proofs and empirical evidence remain unchanged. Smaller loss plots and a new normalized-reward description of BTL that is imprecise relative to Equation (2) temper these gains, but do not outweigh the useful corrections and clarifications.
